clue.text: Feast in the dorm? Take cover!

definitions.meaning: a meal laid out on a bed, a midnight feast in a dormitory
a decorative blanket thrown over a bed

explanation.surface: A warning shouted as a midnight feast in the school dormitory is about to be discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take cover!' sounds like an order to hide, but 'Take' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is food laid out on a bed; as one word it is the blanket covering the bed.

clue.text: Cheese symposium of minimal duration?

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fest is a gathering or festival, like a symposium, a convivial meeting

explanation.surface: A cheese conference that is over almost as soon as it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of short: lasting the least time of all.

clue.text: Flirt with daughter's friend

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with their daughter's friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to toy amorously, trifle with someone's affections.

clue.text: Meal for which electric toaster's used?

definitions.text: Meal for which electric toaster's used?

parts.words: Meal for which electric toaster's used?
parts.note: a joke on the first meal of the day cooked with mains electricity, when really it is a working breakfast for executives

explanation.surface: A question about which meal needs the electric toaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday reading is about kitchen appliances; the real phrase is a business meeting held over breakfast by influential people.
explanation.definitionFit: A business meeting held over an early meal, the energy pun standing for influence and authority.

clue.text: Leaks sometimes contemplated by insiders

definitions.meaning: ... of gas or liquid through a gap
insiders read as prisoners, who dream of breaking out of jail

explanation.surface: Company insiders occasionally think about leaking information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insiders' suggests people inside an organisation leaking secrets, but here they are people inside a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas or water seepages are both called that, and so are prison breakouts that inmates plan.

clue.text: Theatre worker's right, being cared for by doctor

parts.note: esse is Latin for 'to be', used in English for being or existence

explanation.surface: A patient's right to be looked after by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cared for by doctor' means the doctor's abbreviation comes first, with the other pieces after it; esse is the Latin infinitive 'to be', borrowed into English philosophy for being.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre dresser helps actors into their costumes backstage.

clue.text: the studio?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'the studio? (4)' is cut short by OCR: the opening words carrying the definition and wordplay for ETCH are missing, and a search of the text found nothing.

clue.text: Scholastic term for residents of the New World?

definitions.text: Scholastic term for residents of the New World?

parts.words: Scholastic term for residents of the New World?
parts.note: a school period of three months, the word Americans use for a division of the academic year

explanation.surface: Asking what American students call their school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'residents of the New World' means Americans, in whose schools and colleges the year is split into three such periods.
explanation.definitionFit: In North American education an academic term lasting about three months is called this.

clue.text: Insect found among vetch or nettles

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words vetch or nettles

explanation.surface: A wasp discovered among weeds and wild plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stinging wasp is called this.

clue.text: Classes having demonstration before dismissal

indicators.note: places the marching part ahead of the classes

parts.note: people having a demonstration are protesters out marching
orders are classes or ranks, as in social orders

explanation.surface: School classes are given a demonstration before being dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given notice to leave, an idiom for being sacked or sent packing.

clue.text: Relative in US city meets wife

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A relative in an American city meets up with a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer written with a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage, such as a spouse's parent.

clue.text: Charles Edward or Maurice?

definitions.meaning: Charles Edward Stuart, Bonnie Prince Charlie, was called the Young Pretender's knightly title, the Young (title)
Maurice, the French singer and actor of Gigi

explanation.surface: Two first names asked about in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie, Charles Edward Stuart, was known as 'the Young' plus this title; Maurice was the French entertainer famous for 'Thank Heaven for Little Girls'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a knight, a title for the Stuart prince and the surname of the Parisian singer.

clue.text: Ply raft constructed in specialised plant

indicators.note: something constructed is put together anew, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A raft of plywood is built in a dedicated factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnivorous plant, such as the Venus variety, that catches insects.

clue.text: Produce from East Caribbean, found in exotic trees

indicators.note: places the abbreviations inside the rearranged letters
exotic suggests strange and foreign, so the letters of trees are made unfamiliar by reordering

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
C is a short form for Caribbean

explanation.surface: A product of the eastern Caribbean, discovered in tropical trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges TREES to SRETE, and 'found in' sets EC inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to produce and discharge a substance, as a gland does.

clue.text: Avoiding of excesses in terms of personal ties?

definitions.meaning: read literally as the bonds one places on oneself

explanation.surface: Explaining moderation as a matter of personal bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in terms of' links the two definitions; the second is a playful literal reading of the hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control, keeping one's appetites in check, as if tying oneself up.

clue.text: Produce a number of acts?

parts.note: sounds like staging a play in several acts, but the acts are laws of Parliament

explanation.surface: A question about staging a play in several acts.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatrical reading is a decoy: the acts are statutes, which a legislature produces.
explanation.definitionFit: To make laws, and laws passed by Parliament are called Acts.

clue.text: Order restricting church is offensive

indicators.note: the order hems in the church, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A decree limiting the church is objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: An indent in British usage is an official requisition or order for supplies; the church abbreviation is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means improper or shocking, giving offence to decency.

clue.text: Wrestling club offering to board?

parts.note: grappling is wrestling, struggling hand to hand
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A wrestling club making an offer to its committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a committee, but it means boarding an enemy ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooked tool thrown to hold an enemy ship alongside so sailors can climb aboard.

clue.text: Manage to turn into lay-by

definitions.meaning: steer a vehicle off the road into a stopping place; a lay-by is a British roadside parking area

explanation.surface: A driver manages to steer into a roadside stopping place.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring off a feat, and also a roadside area where motorists can stop.

clue.text: Change ends, in a manner of speaking?

definitions.text: Change ends, in a manner of speaking?

parts.words: Change ends, in a manner of speaking?
parts.note: sounds like teams swapping halves of a pitch, but means altering word endings or modulating the voice

explanation.surface: Teams swapping sides at half-time, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting picture is a decoy: grammar alters the endings of words to show tense or number, and speakers vary their pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a word is varied at its ending for tense or case, and a voice is modulated in tone.

clue.text: Breaches of trust revealed in article on public transport

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
buses are public transport

explanation.surface: Betrayals exposed in a newspaper article about buses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts A above BUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuses of power or position that betray those who trusted it.

clue.text: Grumpy companion shunning limelight?

definitions.meaning: Grumpy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, and another is shy

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered friend who keeps out of the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grumpy' looks like an adjective, but it is the name of one of Snow White's seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow dwarf of Grumpy, and an adjective for shy, retiring people.

clue.text: What's found in stokehold in vessel in front

indicators.note: the vessel goes in the front, one piece inside the other

parts.note: face means front, as in the face of a building
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Something found in a ship's boiler room, in a vessel at the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship given the stokehold, but it is an urn. A stokehold is where a ship's boilers are fed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's stokehold holds the enclosed fire where fuel is burnt to heat the boilers.

clue.text: Excuse for failure in Latin

parts.note: a pretext for not having done something, whose name comes from a Latin word meaning elsewhere

explanation.surface: An excuse for flunking a Latin exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests failing at Latin; the point is that the word for an excuse is itself Latin, meaning 'elsewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere, extended to any excuse; the Latin word means 'in another place'.

clue.text: TV programme's ethos, not exactly hard rock

parts.note: a soap is a TV soap opera, with its possessive giving the S
tone is the prevailing character or ethos

explanation.surface: A TV soap's character is hardly heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard rock' suggests music, but it is mineral: this rock is soft enough to carve.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc-rich steatite is soft and easily carved, so it is far from a hard stone.

clue.text: Suppress primitive instincts in middle of melee

indicators.note: the instincts are set within the central letters
takes the central letters of the word melee

parts.note: the id is the Freudian seat of primitive instincts

explanation.surface: Holding back basic urges in the thick of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' drops only the first and last letters of melee, leaving three; the id is Freud's term for the unconscious seat of primitive drives.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit or slur over a sound or syllable, suppressing it in speech.

clue.text: Part found in outbuilding

definitions.meaning: separate from, cast off, as a tree drops leaves
a simple hut in a garden

explanation.surface: A component discovered in a garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a noun but is the verb, to let go of; 'found in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off or separate from something, and a simple wooden hut for storage.

clue.text: Type to be influenced by charm, thief sits entranced

definitions.text: Type to be influenced by charm

indicators.note: someone entranced is carried away from their normal state, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A thief sits spellbound, the sort swayed by charms.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is a charm or object of devotion, and someone in thrall to one is so called.
